2.5.1 GENERAL INTRODUCTION
Bryophytes (Greek, bryon-moss, phyton-plant) are
essentially small plants from a few millimeters to a few
centimeters. Bryophytes are photosynthetic, non-vascular,
true embryophytes and were among the first plants that
lived in the water and settled in terrestrial environment.

They inhabit almost all ecosystems on the earth. The geographical ranges are wider than those of vascular plants due to the long distance dispersal of small spores, huge survival rate and settling specific microhabitats over the huge areas.

2.5.2 CHARACTERISTICS FEATURES OF BRYOPHYTES Some of the basic features of bryophytes are given below:
1. Bryophytes usually grow on damp, moist and shady places. They form a green carpet on damp soil, rocks, walls and barks of trees.

2. The plant body lacks true roots, stems or leaves and may have root-like, stem like or leaf like structure. The plant body may be flat as in liverworts or tiny erect leafy structures on stalks, as in mosses.
3. The plant body of bryophytes is gametophyte since it produces gametes. It is an independent, autotrophic and haploid.

4. The plant body is attached to the substratum by unicellular or multicellular rhizoids. 5. The plant body is made up of simple parenchymatous cells. Vascular tissues are absent. 6. Reproduction takes place by vegetative and sexual method. 7. Vegetative reproduction takes place by fragmentation, adventitious buds, gemmae etc. 8. Sexual reproduction is oogamous type (i.e. female gamete is larger and im-motile

whereas, male gamete is smaller and motile). 9. The male sex organ is known as antheridium that produces biflagellate male gamete called antherozoids while female sex organ is flask shaped archegonium that produces a single egg (oosphere). 10. The antherozoids are released in water and come in contact with archegonium and get fused with egg to form diploid zygote (oospore). 11. The zygote produces multicellular body called sporophyte. The sporophyte is parasitic over gametophyte for nutrition and attachment. 12. The sporophyte produces spores. On germination, these spores give rise to gametophytic stage. 13. The life cycle of bryophyte show alternation of generation.
2.5.3 CLASSIFICATION

The division bryophyta has been divided into three classes: 1. Hepaticopsida (Liverworts) The name hepaticopsida comes from the word ‘hepatic’ which means liver. So, ‘Hepaticopsida’ literally means ‘class of liver like plants. The main characteristic features are given below: i. The plant body is gametophyte which is dorsoventral and may be thalloid or foliose (i.e. differentiated into leaves and stem like structures). Leaf, if present, are without mid-rib. ii. The ventral surface of thallus is provided with scales and rhizoids. Rhizoids are unicellular and unbranched. iii. Sex organs are borne on dorsal side of the thallus embedded in tissues. iv. The sporophyte may be simple, or differentiated into foot and capsule, or into a foot, seta and capsule. v. The sporophyte is completely dependent on gametophyte for its nutrition. vi. The columella is absent in the capsule. vii. Spores germinate to produce gametophytic plant body. A distinct protonema stage is absent. Examples: Marchantia, Riccia, Porella, etc.
